title: Edit a strategy — compose, compile, review, apply

data.name: sectionOptions
data.shape: { kind: 'strategy-missing' | 'strategy-unreadable' | 'vocabulary-unreadable' | 'ready', detail?: { summary: Strategy, sections }, templates?, categories?, limits?: { maxResultBytes, deadlineMs } }
data.source: app.readSectionOptions.execute — one read that answers strategy, current sections, and the platform's section vocabulary together

data.name: compiled
data.source: app.compilePlan.execute — effect-free by platform design; the intent is built by updateCompileIntent, the same domain builder the conformance guard calls

data.name: proposal
data.shape: { kind: 'proposal' | 'refused', proposal?: { confirmationToken, consequence }, reason?: string }

data.name: problem
data.source: searchParams — the reason a refused apply redirected back with. The action rebuilds `?compile=1&tagline=…&sections=…&problem=` from the values the apply form carried (PlanReviewPanel's `carry`), so the bounce lands on a freshly recompiled review rather than a blank compose

components.purpose: Compose a change to a strategy — tagline and report sections — ask BattleGrid what it would do, and decide from the answer.

actions.effect: GET ?compile=1&tagline=…&sections=…&unknownSections=… — compiles and replaces the compose form with the review. Writes nothing.
Server action: applies the reviewed plan exactly as compiled, reconfigures bound agents, redirects to /strategies

components.current_implementation: Server component with eight render branches, each a full-page <main>. Page headings at text-2xl (raised from xl when DT-0002 showed h1 and the panel h2 the same size). The compose branch is a method=get form carrying the tagline input AND a sections checklist grouped by platform category, with the platform's preview limits sentence when published, and hidden inputs round-tripping sections the vocabulary does not recognise. A 'Back to <strategy>' link is held once and rendered on the five post-read branches. The compile submit wears BUTTON_SECONDARY deliberately — the only primary in this flow is the review's Apply. Form treatments come from the CONTROL/LABEL/CHECKBOX/BUTTON_* constants in control.ts. DT-0015 landed on this page and closed the needs-redesign it was carrying: the compose branch's bound-agent sentence now wears the same clothes it wears on the review — rounded-gc-2 border border-consequence-border bg-consequence-subtle p-4 when one or more agents would be reconfigured, an unchanged plain `mt-1 text-sm font-medium` sentence when the count is zero; `compile-rejected` renders BattleGrid's reason on border-danger-default/bg-danger-subtle with role=alert kept and 'Nothing was changed.' on border-quiet-border/bg-quiet-subtle beside it (absence committed, never sharing danger's palette), its two links keeping their order and text-link treatment; `vocabulary-unavailable` renders its explanation on border-notice-border/bg-notice-subtle with role=alert kept; and the single exits on strategy-not-found, strategy-unreadable and vocabulary-unavailable are anchors wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY rather than underlined text. `strategy-unreadable` still shows no reason — the read result carries none up to this page; that is behavior and is tracked as backlog `strategy-unreadable-arrives-without-a-reason`, deliberately not restyled around. Both unreadable branches now render the read's own reason and WhyNotLoaded — they rendered a heading and a back link until the query stopped dropping them. Since `a-refusal-lands-where-someone-reads-it` (#240) every render branch mounts the shared `<CarriedProblem problem={problem} />` — this page minted `?problem=` on a refused apply and never read the parameter (the defect #240 was filed on); it now reads it on all branches, and the apply's bounce road is `backToReview`: the action rebuilds `compile=1&…&problem=` from the hidden values the apply form carried, so a refused apply lands on a recompiled review with the refusal above it rather than on a compose form that forgot the work.
constraints: The zero-agent and one-or-more-agent forms of the compose blast radius must stay visually different — DT-0015 made the reached case a consequence block and left the zero case a plain sentence precisely because they are different acts, and flattening them back to one treatment loses that.

`compile-rejected`'s 'Nothing was changed.' must not be pulled into the reason's palette — danger and quiet sit adjacent here on purpose (system principle: absence gets the same visual commitment as a warning, without borrowing danger's colour).
`vocabulary-unavailable` takes notice, not danger — it is a refusal to proceed, not a failed attempt (DT-0004's refusal-to-mint precedent); nothing on it may be styled as retryable.

The compile control must keep saying what it does and does not do — 'Compile — see what this would do, without doing it'. Compiling is effect-free by platform design (openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:34-37, 'Compiling MUST NOT alter a strategy, and the interface MUST NOT present compiling and applying as equivalent actions')

The compile submit is secondary on purpose — two accent buttons in one journey would put the same weight on looking and on doing (openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:50-54, 'applying is presented as the act with consequences and compiling as the act without'). A design must not promote it to primary
The bound-agent count must appear above the fields on the compose branch, before the user edits — not only on the review
Compiling is a GET and must stay one: shareable, re-runnable by URL, and never a POST that implies commitment

vocabulary-unavailable must remain a full-page refusal, not a dismissible banner over a usable form — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:386-389 ('WHEN the vocabulary cannot be read from BattleGrid THEN the section checklist is not shown AND the user is told why composing is not available')

strategy-unreadable must stay distinguishable from strategy-not-found — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:329-332 ('the user is told it could not be loaded AND this is distinguished from a strategy that does not exist')

compile-rejected must keep the sentence 'Nothing was changed.' — after a failure the user's first question is whether it was partial. BattleGrid's reason is shown verbatim and usually names what to fix, so 'Compose a different change' is offered before the way back
review-apply-refused still renders the full review; the refusal reason usually names what to change, and hiding the review would strand the user

The 'Back to <strategy>' link must survive on every branch that has a strategy to go back to — the page once rendered no way back to the strategy being edited. The three pre-read branches cannot name one and offer a BUTTON_SECONDARY exit to the roster or the strategy id instead (DT-0015)

components.purpose: Edit the one-line description the strategy carries.
components.current_implementation: A single text input pre-filled with the current tagline, wearing the CONTROL constant, its label wearing LABEL. Compiling with it unchanged is legitimate — the intent summary then names only the sections.
constraints: Control and label treatments come from the CONTROL and LABEL constants in control.ts, shared product-wide — not a per-page className.

components.purpose: Choose which report sections the strategy includes, from what the platform publishes today.

actions.effect: Checks or unchecks a section; nothing happens until compile

components.current_implementation: A fieldset of native checkboxes grouped into sub-fieldsets by the platform's categories (legend at text-xs uppercase), with templates the platform returned without a category in a trailing ungrouped block. Sections the strategy currently includes are pre-checked. Above the boxes: a pointer to the section library ('What each section reads … is in the section library'). Sections the strategy contains that the vocabulary does not recognise ride as hidden inputs so a compile round-trips them unchanged. Since DT-0015 each box wears the shared `CHECKBOX` constant from control.ts — `accent-accent-default`, accent-color and nothing else, so the browser keeps drawing the box and its checked/indeterminate/disabled/forced-colors states — and each label row is `flex min-h-control items-center gap-2 text-sm tablet:min-h-0`: the 44px tap-target floor on touch, the previous density back from the 768px `tablet` breakpoint up. Both the grouped and the ungrouped block carry the identical row and box treatment.
constraints: The checkbox treatment is `CHECKBOX` in control.ts and is accent-color only by decision (DT-0015) — a design that replaces the native box has to re-implement four states the browser already renders correctly, including forced-colors

The 44px row floor is mobile-only on purpose — `min-h-control` with `tablet:min-h-0` above 768px; a design must not drop the touch floor, and must not push the desktop rows to 44px either, since DT-0015 explicitly preserved desktop density

Current sections are pre-selected — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:355-359 ('each section the strategy currently includes is shown as selected AND available sections the strategy does not currently include are shown as deselected')

Grouping follows the categories BattleGrid returns — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:361-365; the list is discovered at edit time, never fixed at build time (spec.md:339-343), so a design cannot assume a stable set or count of groups

The hidden unknownSections inputs are behavior, not presentation — dropping them silently discards sections the vocabulary does not recognise. A design must not remove or surface-as-editable what it cannot name
The section-library link must stay with the checklist — it answers the question an author has while ticking boxes

components.purpose: State the ceilings a preview of this composition runs under, where the platform publishes them.
components.current_implementation: A text-xs text-text-secondary sentence inside the sections fieldset: max result bytes (localized) and deadline in seconds, ending 'Past either, BattleGrid refuses the preview rather than truncating it.' Rendered only when the platform publishes limits; nothing is substituted when it does not.
constraints: Shown while composing, stated as what would be refused rather than truncated — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:345-349 and :367-370

When the platform publishes no ceiling, none is shown and no default is substituted — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:372-374 ('a limit this product invented would be read as the platform's and composed against'). An empty state for this component must stay empty

components.purpose: Show exactly what applying would do, and let the user apply from inside that review rather than beside it.

actions.effect: POSTs the reviewed plan and its confirmation token. Reconfigures every bound agent immediately, then redirects to /strategies.
Anchor back to the compose form (absolute href, required by the component) to change the intent

components.current_implementation: Styled per DT-0002, with its buttons now drawn from the shared BUTTON_PRIMARY/BUTTON_SECONDARY constants in control.ts (which lifted DT-0002's strings verbatim and added DT-0004's hover/active). Consequence-toned blast radius with a 4px left border, notice-toned concerns block that shares no colour with danger, quiet-toned summary, accent (not danger) apply button with 'Go back and change it' as a bordered peer. Refusal states render a role=alert paragraph and no control at all. Since `a-refusal-lands-where-someone-reads-it` (#240) the panel takes `carry` — the composed tagline, sections and unknownSections ride the apply form as hidden inputs, purely so a refused apply can rebuild the compile URL and land on a recompiled review; `carry` is absent when the apply was refused before it could be offered, because that confirmation is known-dead and re-showing its panel would invite a second press of a button that cannot succeed.
constraints: There must be no control on this surface that applies without a review having been rendered first — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:50-54 ('applying is not reachable without a compiled result to apply'). Applying is an act performed *from* a review, never a button beside a compile button (design S-G)
'Nothing has changed yet' must remain the first thing read. It is the sentence that makes an effect-free compile legible as effect-free
The apply button's label carries the consequence ('reconfigures N agents now') and must not be shortened to a bare verb

Concerns are advisory and must never be presented as blockers — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:138-141 ('Grid-Commander SHALL show them and permit the user to proceed. It MUST NOT refuse an application the platform would accept')

The BattleGrid-authored `consequence` string is stored with the token so the audit can prove what was shown; it must be displayed verbatim and must not be paraphrased, truncated, or collapsed behind a disclosure
The review must still render when apply is refused — the reason usually names what to change
[concerns-panel] The disclaimer sentence ('These do not prevent the change. They describe how the strategy is set up.') must not be dropped or demoted — without it the panel reads as a blocker
[concerns-panel] Must not adopt error styling. A one-word tagline edit can return two concerns while viable is true; styling them as failures would train users to abandon valid edits
[concerns-panel] Count in the heading must stay, so the user knows the list is complete

[apply-confirmation] The hidden `plan` field carries the reviewed plan rather than recompiling — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:56-59 ('apply only a plan the platform itself compiled, exactly as compiled'). A design must not move, defer, or re-derive this value
[apply-confirmation] The blocked and not-viable states are role=alert paragraphs that replace the button entirely; there must be no disabled-looking apply control that suggests retrying will help
[apply-confirmation] 'Go back and change it' must remain a visible peer of Apply, not a hidden or tertiary escape — it is the expected outcome of a review that surprised the user
Buttons take their treatment from the BUTTON_PRIMARY/BUTTON_SECONDARY constants in control.ts, shared product-wide — not a per-panel className

components.purpose: State how many agents this change reaches, as its own claim rather than a clause in a sentence.
components.current_implementation: Three visually distinct treatments. reaches-agents: consequence block with 4px left border, count at text-xl/semibold on its own line, role=alert. reaches-none: a single quiet line, no border, no fill. unknown: notice block with 4px left border, role=alert, deliberately block-shaped so it cannot be mistaken for zero.
constraints: Must stay its own block. Five bound agents is a different act from zero and must not have to be read for — folding it into a sentence is the specific failure this component exists to prevent

`null` (BattleGrid did not report) must remain visibly distinct from `0` (nothing is bound) — openspec/specs/strategy-authoring/spec.md:30-32 makes zero a stated case, and rendering the unknown case as zero would understate the risk
The note that open positions are reported for awareness and do not block must stay with the count

components.purpose: List what would actually differ, and say plainly when nothing would.
components.current_implementation: Bordered bg-bg-raised block: 'What would change' heading plus a disc list; a single sentence when the list is empty; the proposed revision as a trailing sentence when reported.
constraints: The empty case must keep its own sentence ('Nothing — this plan leaves the strategy as it is') rather than rendering an empty list; a compile that changes nothing is a real and useful outcome
The proposed revision number is what the user will see on the roster afterwards and must stay legible next to the changes

components.purpose: Turn away a request that has no authority, and say how to fix it.
components.current_implementation: Shared NotConnected component (require-connection.tsx): h1 + message, and since DT-0006 the connect link is an anchor wearing BUTTON_SECONDARY — the way in as a target, not a sentence, at the 44px floor with secondary's hover. Used by every authenticated page, so this treatment is inherited everywhere.
constraints: One page for every cause; they differ in cause and not in remedy (design W-C) — a design must not invent per-cause variants

flows.name: Change tagline and sections, then apply
steps: open editor, read blast radius above the fields
edit tagline, tick and untick sections (current ones pre-checked)
read 'Nothing has changed yet', blast radius, changed axes, concerns

flows.name: Compile, then think better of it
steps: compose form again at the strategy's current state

flows.name: Compile something the platform refuses
steps: Compose a different change, or back to the strategy

accessibility.notes: Review section is labelled by `review-heading`. Blast radius (reached and unknown cases), the consequence sentence, the vocabulary-unavailable reason, the compile-rejected reason, and both apply-refusal states are role=alert; the plan summary is role=status. The compose branch's bound-agent sentence carries no role — it is read in document order above the fields. Sections are native checkboxes inside nested fieldsets with legends, tinted by accent-color only so the browser's own checked/indeterminate/disabled/forced-colors rendering survives; each label row meets the 44px tap floor below the tablet breakpoint. Compiling is a full page navigation, so the review is reached by normal document order rather than a live region.
